analysis: Examined StatusCommand.swift head 135-140: status now displays authorization via new DaemonState.displayedProviderAuthorization (presumably tolerant of a late renewal while the lease is unexpired) and passes a separate removalAuthorization from currentProviderAuthorization into ProviderAuthorizationReadiness.summary. This is display-only CLI output in the operator's own process; it grants no serving permission, so T-052/T-053 (stale authorization surviving) are not affected on the coordinator side. The MDM-removal gating path in UnenrollCommand+KeepServing.swift (head 21-27, 61-67) still uses currentProviderAuthorization and removalReady both before and after profile inspection; the only change passes the same authorization as removalAuthorization to summary for its error text, so the T-057 premature-MDM-removal guard is unchanged. New test (StatusCommandRunTests head 253-279) asserts that a late renewal shows App Attest but says 'MDM removal needs fresh coordinator readiness' and does not suggest unenroll, i.e. summary must base removal guidance on removalAuthorization. Integration questions (implementations not supplied): verify displayedProviderAuthorization still enforces coordinator URL binding and expiresAt (lease not expired) and does not display authorization for a revoked/disconnected session; verify summary(_:removalAuthorization:now:) only offers removal guidance when removalAuthorization is removal-ready, so displayed-but-stale grants never steer an operator to remove MDM (T-057, TB-011). No regression identified in supplied code.
